claims.claim: Unreachable normalization anchors compress legitimate scores below 21.021/100.
claims.witness: real unchanged (agent-10, agent-40, agent-33, agent-1 of the Opus run); synthetic controls: grid-only greedy, invalid

arms.label: good control: grid-only greedy, current judge
real agent-10, tester stop removed, same anchors

claims.fix_tested: two: linear 3418..92304 moves agent-10 by +78.94 and keeps order; removing the tester's undocumented 2*N*N stop on the same anchors moves it by +15.83 and reorders real runs (agent-1 below agent-10 under the cap, 91007 vs about 92040 raw; above its best run without it, 164473 vs 158357)
claims.correct_work_keeps_score: no, every scale change moves scores up; invalid stays 0, starter stays 0, and greedy keeps 3.04 with the stop removed (it never reaches the cap)
claims.note: Real runs do reach the ceiling: all 87 archived reports (53 files) sit at 20.46-21.02 and the stop binds 47-50 of 50 cases, so the cap hides real differences; weakest point: the four measured runs read the destination list from stdin (a text match finds it in all 53 files) although the README says solutions read only the grid (a grid-only greedy never reaches the cap, 3.04), replay of the longest uncapped case hits the tester's 60 s limit in some repeats, and the choice of fix is discretionary.
